headline: Oil Cools and Gold Firms as Wall Street Digests a Chip-Led Rout
body_html:
U.S. stocks start the week with investors weighing a lopsided Friday session against a calmer tone in energy. Crude eased about 3% on hopes that Qatari-led talks could bring the Iran war to a close, and gold edged higher as traders parsed signals from the Federal Reserve.

Friday, October 30, was rougher than the headline moves suggest: 343 of the 530 stocks we track fell, while 183 rose. Semiconductors were the clear weak spot, down 6.04% on average, with Sandisk off 13.47% and Coherent down 11.34%. Materials, industrials and healthcare also slipped, while homebuilders gained 1.75% and energy added 0.45%.

At the open, watch whether chip selling extends or steadies, and whether software and internet names hit hard Friday, such as Roblox, Twilio and Datadog, attract buyers. Oil remains the swing factor, as diplomatic hopes sit against Iranian naval claims that two tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Abroad, the Bank of England is expected to raise rates, with attention on whether it tempers bets on further increases.

briefs.headline: Chip stocks take the brunt of Friday's selling
briefs.body: Semiconductors fell 6.04% on average on Friday, the steepest drop among the sectors we track. Sandisk lost 13.47% and Coherent dropped 11.34%. The open will show whether buyers step in or the pressure carries into a new week.

briefs.headline: Software and internet names sharply lower
briefs.body: Roblox sank 18.05%, Twilio fell 15.24% and Datadog slid 11.5% on Friday, dragging software down 1.14% on average. Bright Horizons also dropped 17.92%. Traders will look for signs of stabilization in these battered shares.

briefs.headline: Housing-linked shares buck the decline
briefs.body: Homebuilders were the best sector on Friday, up 1.75% on average. Cavco Industries jumped 13.11% and flooring maker Mohawk Industries gained 7.25%. Whether housing-related strength holds as the broader market wobbles is a theme to track.

briefs.headline: Capri and GoDaddy lead the winners
briefs.body: Capri Holdings rose 16.31% on Friday, the biggest gain in our universe. GoDaddy added 10.72%, Donnelley Financial 9.53% and CoStar Group 7.21%. Gains like these were rare, with only 183 of 530 stocks finishing higher.

briefs.headline: Oil slips as Iran peace hopes build
briefs.body: Crude fell about 3% on optimism that Qatari-led negotiations could end the Iran war. Still, Iran's naval force said two tankers exploded after hitting mines in Hormuz, a reminder that supply risks remain. Energy stocks added 0.45% on Friday.

briefs.headline: Bank of England seen ready to lift rates
briefs.body: The Bank of England is expected to raise interest rates, though it may resist market bets on further increases. Gold rose as softer oil eased some inflation worries and investors weighed Fed signals. Rate commentary could steer sentiment at the open.
